citation: Stewart ML, Zimmer JP (2017). A High Fiber Cookie Made with Resistant Starch Type 4 Reduces Post-Prandial Glucose and Insulin Responses in Healthy Adults. Nutrients 9(3):237.
protocol: Two cookies, double-blind crossover: control cookie vs fibre cookie with RS4 (VERSAFIBE 1490), both 36.84 g total carbohydrate, ~4 g fat, ~5 g protein; available carbohydrate 36.3 vs 12.7 g, fibre 0.55 vs 24.1 g. Venous and capillary blood at 0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120 min.
population: n=28 healthy adults (14 men, 14 women), age 42.8 ± 18.5 y, BMI 24.7 ± 3.3 kg/m2 (Table 2, mean ± SD).

reports.where: Table 3: iAUC0-120 and Cmax, venous and capillary, per cookie
Table 3: serum insulin iAUC0-120 and Cmax per cookie, pmol/L·h

note: Paired-meal contrast, fibre: control cookie vs RS4 high-fibre cookie at matched total carbohydrate, fat and protein. Total carbohydrate matched, so the fibre swap lowers available carbohydrate; the model should see this as fibre in total carbohydrate. Watch: n differs by marker (footnote), Cmax rows carry a mis-pasted "·h" unit. Only in figures: glucose and insulin time courses.
